title: Guards Audit
eyebrow: Audit for approval · issue 285, "Guards block only unrecoverable actions" · nothing changed yet

short.lead: I went through every hook in hook.py that can stop me, against your test: only data loss with no way back should stop me. Seven kinds of action keep asking or stay refused, deletes ask only when the data isn't saved, four refusals become reminders, and the background-work guard goes completely. Publishing a page is never refused again.
short.hint: Tap a card for what it guards today and what changes.
items: Seven kinds of action that still stop me

Pushing or committing to main stays refused. Asking first stays for: force-push, --all or --mirror push; deleting a branch, local (branch -D) or remote (push --delete); git clean and filter-branch; reset, checkout -- and restore while uncommitted work exists; stash drop and clear; truncating a file.
Nothing; these already match your test.
Deletes ask only when the file isn't saved

Today every rm asks, even for a committed file git can restore. After this, a delete asks only when it is recursive (rm -r, rmdir /s, Remove-Item -Recurse) or when a file it deletes has uncommitted changes or was never committed. Deleting a committed, unchanged file runs without asking.
Background work, kills and branch commits stop asking

These no longer ask: background or hidden commands (nohup, a trailing &, Start-Process, background jobs), piping a wait through tail or head, killing a process, and commits, merges or rebases on my own branch when the folder isn't clear. The "Never hide work" rule text goes too, and so does its 5-minute stall-check reminder.

First, publishing a page not built by make_page.py: today it is denied, afterwards it goes through with a reminder. Second, Claude credit or a claude/ branch on GitHub, and an issue without its sections: denied, afterwards a reminder. Third, a third helper or a helper's own helper: denied, afterwards a reminder. Fourth, overwriting a whole file: today it always asks; afterwards it asks only when that file has uncommitted changes.

Today one unanswered prompt makes every later prompt in the session refuse at once. That cascade blocked both page publishes and the commit. After this, the timer only acts on prompts the guards above raise, never on others such as publishing a page. Each prompt waits on its own, and nothing is refused just because an earlier one went unanswered.
The design-loop lock stops code edits until you approve a build plan. It stopped a builder today, but it is also what makes plans reach you as a page first. Choose below.
Your answer in the Choices section.

choices: What should the design-loop lock do?
Code edits go through, with a reminder that the plan hasn't been approved. It matches your test, but nothing forces the page step.
Plans always reach you first, but builders stall while you're away.
It doesn't protect data, so your test says reminder; the cost is that the plan step becomes a habit rather than a gate.
Force-pushing to my own branch (not main): ask, or allow?
Old commits stay in the local history (reflog), so it can be undone on this machine.
Safer if you ever push to my branches too.
Force-pushing to main stays refused either way.
